question.text: Which of the following correctly describes an interim dividend?

answer.text: A dividend that is declared but never actually paid to shareholders
A dividend declared during the year, as opposed to the final dividend usually declared at year-end
A dividend paid only to preference shareholders during the year
A dividend declared at the Annual General Meeting after audited results

explanation.text: The Logic: Dividends declared during the year are called interim dividends, in contrast to the final dividend that is usually declared at the year-end. The Trap: Candidates may confuse interim and final dividends, or assume specific procedural requirements (such as Board-only approval or pre-finalization-of-accounts conditions) that are not stated in the source. Note: The distinction between interim and final dividends in the workbook is timing-based — interim is during the year, final is at year-end.
